communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

A copy of any inventory or accounting of the papers in James Jesus Angleton's office, desk, home or other storage system under his control, such as restricted safes or secure filing cabinets located at CIA, at the time or in the aftermath of his resignation, as well as any reports or memos discussing with the issue.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Emma Best

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Official Military Personnel File (OMPF) concerning subject below
Name of Veteran: Earl Glenn Hayes
Branch: United States Navy
DOB: August 17, 1960
Dates of Service: 1978 to 1984
Date of Death: February 13, 1984

please provide the following documents:
1) History of Assignments NAVPERS form 601-5
2) all Navy Occupational training history NAVPERS 601-4 , Cumulative transfers and receipts NAVPERS 601-12, 
3) Navy Unit Commendation citation award
4) list of awards, decorations, Badges
5) Military Education, training courses
6) Dates of service, dates of ranks, campaigns 

Awards include Navy Commendation Medal, Navy Unit Commendation, Navy good conduct medal, Expert Rifle Ribbon. NEC 5326 Combatant Swimmer. 

Obituary
https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-pantagraph-earl-hayes-obituary-1984/7587918/?locale=en-US

First name: Earl
Middle initial: G

DOB 8/17/1960

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Eric Bradley

communications.subject: Washington Public Records Act Request: Organized Retail Crime Task Force: Auror
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Records related to the Organized Retail Crime Theft Task Force announced on June 23, 2022, specifically concerning the implementation, use, and discussion of Auror's crime intelligence platform.

1. All contracts, MOUs, RFPs, or service agreements between the AG's Office and Auror Inc. (auror.co) dated June 23, 2022, to present
1a. Amendments, scope-of-work documents, or SLA agreements related to Auror's services
1b. Invoices, payment receipts, or procurement documents for Auror software/services

2. Budget allocations specific to Auror platform implementation
2a. Documentation of federal/state grants used to fund Auror-related expenditures

3. Training manuals, guides, or protocols for Auror platform use by task force members
3a. Video recordings of Auror software training sessions
3b. Email communications regarding training schedules or materials

4. All incident reports, intelligence briefings, or case files generated through Auror's platform
4a. Spreadsheets/databases tracking organized retail crime incidents processed via Auror
4b. Performance metrics/reports evaluating Auror's effectiveness (2022-2024)

5. Records of technical malfunctions, data inaccuracies, or security breaches involving Auror
5a. Formal complaints from task force members or partner agencies about Auror's system
5b. Internal audits or third-party assessments of Auror's compliance with state data laws

6. Emails/memos between AG staff and Auror representatives (June 23, 2022-present)
6a. Meeting minutes where Auror platform use was discussed
6b. Correspondence with federal partners (FBI, DHS) regarding Auror data sharing

These records are requested from June 23, 2022, to present; Electronic copies are preferred in their original formats wherever possible, and commonly readable formats such as pdf, mp4, png where conversion is required.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Robin Monks

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: Untitled (San Diego Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

I am requesting incident-level crime data for a research project comparing neighborhood-level crime across large US cities. I am asking for the same kind of extract many departments already publish through their open data portals.

Records requested. One row per reported offense, for offenses occurring between 1 January 2019 and 31 December 2025, with these fields:

the incident, case or report number
the date the offense occurred
the offense description, and the offense code if you have one
the location of the offense, as latitude and longitude

Offense fields. Whatever your system already stores is fine. Something along the lines of NIBRS offense codes and descriptions is ideal, but please do not translate, recode or reclassify anything on my behalf. I am not asking you to do any work beyond exporting the fields as they sit. If your records hold more than one offense description or classification per record (for example a local code, a UCR or NIBRS code, and a plain-text description), please include all of them rather than choosing between them.

Location. If coordinates cannot be released, I will accept a block-level address instead - either "4200 BLOCK OF WYOMING ST" or an address with the house number masked to the hundred block, for example "42XX WYOMING ST". I am not asking for exact street addresses. Several large departments publish location in exactly this masked form, and it is sufficient for my purposes.

No personal information is requested. I am not asking for the name, address, date of birth, race, sex, age or any other identifying detail of any victim, witness, suspect, arrestee or officer. Please withhold all such fields. I am asking only for what the offense was, when it happened, and roughly where.

Format. CSV, or any delimited or database export your records system produces. One file for the whole period is easiest, but annual files are fine.

Cost. Please send me a written estimate before incurring any charge above $50.

If any part of this cannot be released, please release the rest and tell me what was withheld and why.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jonathan Mummolo

title: Flock Safety ALPR Records (Contracts, Audit Logs, SB 34, Communications) (Bellflower Public Safety Department)

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: Flock Safety ALPR Records (Contracts, Audit Logs, SB 34, Communications) (Bellflower Public Safety Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I request the following records concerning any products, services, platforms, sensors, or data feeds of the following categories, whether currently used, previously used, piloted, trialed, or formally considered by this agency, for the period January 1, 2020 through August 19, 2026:

Automated license plate reader ("ALPR") and connected-camera systems — including but not limited to Flock Safety (Flock Group Inc.), Motorola Solutions / Vigilant Solutions (LEARN, PlateSearch), Genetec (AutoVu), Axon / Fusus, Rekor, Leonardo/ELSAG, Neology, and Digital Recognition Network (DRN);
Data-integration, analytics, and "real-time crime center" (RTCC) / "real-time awareness center" (RTAC) platforms — including but not limited to Peregrine Technologies (peregrine.io), Palantir, Fusus (Axon), SoundThinking, and any comparable platform that aggregates, links, or searches across agency data sources; and
Any product beyond ALPR cameras offered by the above vendors (e.g., Flock's Condor PTZ video, FlockOS, Nova, or other data-intelligence products; Peregrine's data-integration or AI/"safety flagging" modules).

Where a term below refers to a Flock-specific feature (e.g., "Organization Audit"), please read it to also request the equivalent record in any other vendor's system.
1. Contracts and procurement. All contracts, master services agreements, order forms, amendments, renewals, statements of work, quotes, proposals, purchase orders, invoices, and payment records with any vendor identified above, including any data-processing addenda / data-processing agreements (DPAs), memoranda of understanding (MOUs), and any competitive-bid waivers or sole-source justifications.
2. Vendor communications. All communications (email, text/SMS, letters, meeting notes, calendar invitations) between agency personnel and representatives of any vendor identified above (including the vendor's @flocksafety.com, @peregrine.io, or equivalent domains), concerning procurement, deployment, configuration, camera or sensor siting, pilot / early-access / free-trial programs, and any product beyond ALPR cameras.
3. Search and audit logs. The complete audit/usage logs showing each search or query, including — for Flock — the "Organization Audit" and "Network Audit" logs (Flock Insights dashboard), and — for any RTCC / data-integration platform (e.g., Peregrine) — the user access and query logs. For each entry, please include all available metadata fields, e.g.: record ID, user name, organization/agency name, date/time of search, license plate or query terms, stated reason, case number, camera count, time frame searched, filters, search type, and any text/AI prompt. Please export in the system's native machine-readable format (CSV/XLSX), not as a PDF printout, and do not strip metadata fields.
4. Hotlist and NCIC configuration (commonly the most important item). Records sufficient to show the full hotlist configuration of any ALPR system, including a screenshot, screen capture, printout, or CSV of the hotlists the agency subscribes to. This specifically includes which FBI NCIC "topics" are enabled and, in particular, whether the "Immigration Violator" file / topic is enabled, and the date any such topic was enabled or disabled. Also include any custom hotlists created by the agency.
5. Data sharing and external / federal access. A list of all external entities with which data is shared or from which it is received, and the settings governing that sharing, including:

The agency's Flock network-sharing settings, and whether "National Lookup" and/or statewide lookup are enabled, with the dates access was granted, modified, or revoked;
All external agencies that can access this agency's data, and all agencies whose data this agency can access, with dates;
Specifically, any access by or sharing with federal agencies — ICE, CBP, HSI, ATF, FBI, DHS — including records of searches those agencies (or other agencies on their behalf) ran against this agency's data;
All MOUs, data-sharing agreements, and network-participation terms (e.g., with a fusion center such as NCRIC), and any restrictions placed on downstream use or re-dissemination.

6. California ALPR statutory records (SB 34 and amendments).

The record of access required by Civil Code § 1798.90.52;
The agency's current ALPR usage and privacy policy required by Civil Code § 1798.90.51 (and, if the agency is an ALPR end-user, its policy under § 1798.90.53);
The results of the annual audit of ALPR searches for compliance with the usage/privacy policy (Civil Code § 1798.90.53), including any assessment of whether non-hotlist data was purged within 30 days of collection;
Any records concerning use of ALPR for immigration-enforcement geolocation or retention beyond 30 days (see Civ. Code § 1798.90.5 et seq., as amended).

7. Camera / sensor deployment and locations. Records sufficient to show the number, type, and locations of all cameras or sensors installed in the jurisdiction (fixed ALPR, mobile ALPR, PTZ/video, gunshot-detection, or other), their installation dates, and any encroachment, right-of-way, or other permits issued for their installation.
8. Data sources integrated into any data-integration / RTCC platform. For any platform identified above (e.g., Peregrine), a list of all data sources, feeds, and databases integrated into or accessible through the platform — for example computer-aided dispatch (CAD), records management systems (RMS), body-worn and in-car camera footage, fixed/traffic/school cameras, ALPR data, jail/booking data, DMV or state databases, and any third-party or commercial data sources — together with any system-configuration or data-source inventory documents.
9. Retention, governance, and training. Records reflecting data-retention periods and deletion practices, access controls (who is authorized to search and what approvals are required), prohibited uses, training materials, and internal policies, standard operating procedures, directives, or general orders governing use of any system identified above.
10. Misuse, breaches, and oversight. Any audits, reports, internal-affairs records, complaints, disciplinary records, or communications concerning suspected or confirmed misuse of any system (including searches for personal, immigration, or reproductive-health-related reasons), and any records of data breaches or security incidents involving the data.
11. Surveillance-use policy and impact reports. Any Surveillance Use Policy, Surveillance Impact Report, Privacy Impact Assessment / Data Protection Impact Assessment, or comparable document required by any applicable local surveillance-oversight ordinance, relating to ALPR, RTCC, or data-integration technology generally or to a specific vendor.
12. Governing-body review. Staff reports, resolutions, meeting agendas, minutes, and presentations to the city council / board of supervisors / oversight body concerning approval, funding, or renewal of any contract identified above.
13. Confirmation of non-use. If the agency has never used, piloted, or contracted for any ALPR, connected-camera, RTCC, or data-integration system of the kind described above, please confirm that in writing.

Format, preservation, and processing

Machine-readable format. Please provide records in their original electronic, machine-readable format with metadata intact (Gov. Code § 7922.570); spreadsheets and logs as CSV/XLSX, not PDF printouts.
Preservation. Because some responsive records (particularly ALPR search/audit logs) may be subject to short retention or automatic deletion, I request that the agency preserve all responsive records — and suspend any automatic purge of responsive audit logs — pending completion of this request.
Segregability and exemption log. If any record is withheld in whole or in part, please identify each record and the specific exemption claimed (Gov. Code § 7922.540), and release all reasonably segregable portions (Gov. Code § 7922.525). Data describing how the system operates and is used — as distinct from information about a specific individual — is generally not exempt investigative material (see ACLU of S. Cal. v. Superior Court (2017) 3 Cal.5th 1032). Personal information may be redacted while still disclosing system-level records.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Christian Whitney

communications.subject: RE: California Public Records Act Request #26-627
communications.communication:
Thank you for the October 14 response and the records in the pick-up folder. I've reviewed them, and the request is not yet complete. Many of its numbered items received no determination, and several records that the produced documents refer to were not included. Please reopen PRA 26-627 and provide a supplemental response on the points below.

1. Items that received no determination

Gov. Code § 7922.535(a) requires the City to state whether it has responsive records for each part of a request. The response did not address the following items, and I ask the City to either produce records or state in writing that none exist:

- Item 3: search and audit logs for PlateRanger or any other ALPR system.
- Item 6: the record of access under Civ. Code § 1798.90.52, the ALPR usage and privacy policy under § 1798.90.51 or .53, and any annual audit results.
- Item 8: data sources integrated into any platform. SoundThinking's proposal (in the Sept. 22, 2025 packet) refers to Motorola CommandAware and Axon Fusus as products "currently used by the City." Please confirm whether the City uses either one.
- Item 9: retention, access-control, and training policies, and any procedures or general orders.
- Item 10: misuse, complaint, or breach records.
- Item 11: any surveillance use policy or impact assessment.
- Item 13: confirmation of non-use. The July 14, 2025 staff report refers to "15 already functioning ALPR's deployed in the City." Please identify the vendor of those cameras and produce records responsive to Items 1–12 for them. If the City has never contracted with or piloted Flock Safety, please confirm that in writing.

2. Specific records referenced in the production but not produced

- The fully executed Agreement File No. 1097, including the executed MSA and addenda. The packet copy has blank signature lines, and the September 23, 2025 email says the agreement would be routed by DocuSign.
- The PlateRanger pilot MOU or evaluation agreement that Mr. McNerney said he submitted on May 22, 2025.
- The attachments to the July 24, 2025 "Coverage Definition Call" thread, including "ALPR Locations (1).kmz" and the ShotSpotter coverage KML file, in native format.
- Installation dates for each camera and sensor, plus the encroachment or right-of-way permits issued for them (Item 7). Only the permit-request emails were produced.
- The locations of ShotSpotter sensors on private property. Only government sites were produced.
- Purchase orders and payment records (Item 1).
- Minutes, resolutions, and presentation materials for the July 14 and September 22, 2025 council items (Item 12).

3. Records the City controls through its vendor

Referring Items 4 and 5 to the Sheriff's Department does not cover the City's own PlateRanger system. I have a separate request pending with the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department, but that request does not relieve the City of its obligation to produce records within its own possession or control.

Under Addendum Two, § 5.C of the City's agreement, "Customer shall own the PlateRanger Operational Data." The City is the contracting customer, and its Director of Public Safety administers the account. Records the City owns or has a contractual right to obtain are public records under Gov. Code § 7920.530 even when a vendor stores them (see City of San Jose v. Superior Court (2017) 2 Cal.5th 608). Please obtain from SoundThinking and produce:

- the PlateRanger audit and search logs;
- the hotlist and NCIC topic configuration, including whether any immigration-related topic is enabled;
- the City's participation status in the Rekor Partner Sharing Network, with dates;
- the list of agencies that can access or have accessed the City's data.

If the City believes it lacks possession or control of these records, please explain why.

4. Withheld records

The response says certain records were withheld as attorney-client privileged. Please identify each one by date, author, recipients, and general subject, so the claim can be evaluated, and release any reasonably segregable portions (Gov. Code § 7922.525). Communications that included SoundThinking personnel are not privileged. Please also provide the names and titles of the persons responsible for the denial, as § 7922.540 requires.

5. Format and preservation

Please produce logs and data in their native machine-readable format (CSV or XLSX) under Gov. Code § 7922.570. Please also confirm that the City has preserved responsive audit logs and suspended any automatic deletion while this request is pending, as asked in my original request.

communications.subject: FOLLOW-UP RESPONSE: PRA 26-627 - FLOCK SAFETY ALPR RECORDS; WHITNEY
communications.communication:
To whom it may concern,



The City of Bellflower provided a response to your public records request on October 14, 2026.



Please review the responsive records at the link previously provided: PRA 26-627 - Pick Up by 10/30/2026<https://urldefense.proofpoint.com/v2/url?u=https-3A__portal.laserfiche.com_Portal_Browse.aspx-3Fid-3D389422-26repo-3Dr-2Dac13a437&d=DwMGaQ&c=euGZstcaTDllvimEN8b7jXrwqOf-v5A_CdpgnVfiiMM&r=ek7N1sQ7cRL3lfTkXjGS3bjll3a_Aq4qfJryi4YWLnI&m=5A9MIClFEzwFhOclXalVyUGUMM-yd1b0jYKHKUhD92IjBUi6imIrEh2Fz0_2BA08&s=WQ654lKZvcpai8f1HGXHI83qjyXAcWJS4pXm9wUzeko&e=>



Your initial request was broken into thirteen items.



Listed below in red font is the response to each item:



1.      1. Contracts and procurement. All contracts, master services agreements, order forms, amendments, renewals, statements of work, quotes, proposals, purchase orders, invoices, and payment records with any vendor identified above, including any data-processing addenda/ data-processing agreements (DPAs), memoranda of understanding (MOUs), and any competitive-bid waivers or sole-source

The City's Agreements, Memoranda of Understanding, and Bids are readily available in the City's Archive: City of Bellflower, City Archive<https://urldefense.proofpoint.com/v2/url?u=https-3A__portal.laserfiche.com_Portal_Browse.aspx-3Fid-3D1-26repo-3Dr-2Dac13a437&d=DwMGaQ&c=euGZstcaTDllvimEN8b7jXrwqOf-v5A_CdpgnVfiiMM&r=ek7N1sQ7cRL3lfTkXjGS3bjll3a_Aq4qfJryi4YWLnI&m=5A9MIClFEzwFhOclXalVyUGUMM-yd1b0jYKHKUhD92IjBUi6imIrEh2Fz0_2BA08&s=TpW4RHF2460rH51onwI9W4O4iWi2_zd7Rutods9EJxw&e=>

Please use the search engine to assist you in narrowing down the scope of the work you are seeking.



2.   Vendor communications. All communications (email, text/SMS, letters, meeting notes, calendar invitations) between agency personnel and representatives of any vendor identified above (including the vendor's @flocksafety.com, @peregrine.io, or equivalent domains), concerning procurement, deployment, configuration, camera or sensor siting, pilot/ early-access / free-trial programs, and any product beyond ALPR cameras.

Please refer to the PRA folder initially issued to you for vendor communications.



3.   Search and audit logs. The complete audit/usage logs showing each search or query, including - for Flock - the "Organization Audit" and "Network Audit" logs (Flock Insights    dashboard), and -for Any RTCC/ data-integration Platform - the user access and query logs. For each entry, please include all available metadata fields -include all available metadata fields, e.g.: record ID, username, organization/agency name, date/time of search, license plate or query terms, stated reason, case number, camera count, time frame searched, filters, search type, and any text/AI prompt. Please export in the system's native machine-readable format (CSV/XLSX), not as a PDF printout, and do not strip metadata fields.

The City has no responsive records to provide.  Please contact the Los Angeles Sheriff's Department for responsive logs and records.



4.   Hotlist and NCIC configuration (commonly the most important item). Records sufficient to show the full hotlist configuration of any ALPR system, including a screenshot, screen capture, printout, or CSV of the hotlists the agency subscribes to. This specifically includes which FBI NCIC "topics" are enabled and, in particular, whether the "Immigration Violator" file/ topic is enabled, and the date any such topic as enabled or disabled. Also include any custom hotlists created by the agency.

The City has no responsive records to provide.  Please contact the Los Angeles Sheriff's Department for responsive logs and records.



5.   Data sharing and external/ federal access. A list of all external entities with which data is shared or from which it is received, and the settings governing that sharing, including:

The agency's Flock network-sharing settings, and whether "National Lookup" and/or statewide lookup are enabled, with the dates access was granted, modified, or revoked; All external agencies that can access this agency's data, and all agencies whose data this agency can access, with dates; Specifically, any access by or sharing with federal agencies -ICE, CBP, HSI, ATF, FBI, DHS - including records of searches those agencies (or other agencies on their behalf) ran against this agency's data; All MOUs, data-sharing agreements, and network-participation terms (e.g., with a fusion center such as NCRIC), and any restrictions placed on downstream use or re-dissemination.

The City has no responsive records to provide.  Please contact the Los Angeles Sheriff's Department for responsive logs and records.



6.   California ALPR statutory records (SB 34 and amendments).

The records of access require-d by C1vil Code § 1798.90.52; The agency's current ALPR usage and privacy policy required by Civil Code § 1798.90.51 (and, if the agency is an ALPR end-user, its policy under§ 1798.90.53); The results of the annual audit of ALPR searches for compliance with the usage/privacy policy (Civil Code § 1798.90.53), including any assessment of whether non-hotlist data was purged within 30 days of collection; Any records concerning use of ALPR for immigration-enforcement geolocation or retention beyond 30 days (see Civ. Code § 1798.90.5 et seq., as amended).

The City has no responsive records to provide.  Please contact the Los Angeles Sheriff's Department for responsive logs and records.



7.   Camera/ sensor deployment and locations. Records sufficient to show the number, type, and locations of all cameras or sensors installed in the jurisdiction (fixed ALPR, mobile ALPR, PTZ/video, gunshot-detection, or other), their installation dates, and any encroachment, right-of-way, or other permits issued for their installation.

The City only has a deployment list of ShotSpotter sensors on city-owned poles; the Excel file was initially provided in the folder, along with a PDF of PlateRanger locations.



8.   Data sources integrated into any data-integration/ RTCC platform. For any platform identified above (e.g., Peregrine), a list of all data sources, feeds, and databases integrated into or accessible through the platform - for example computer-aided dispatch (CAD), records management systems (RMS), body-worn and in-car camera footage, fixed/traffic/school cameras, ALPR data, jail/booking data, DMV or state databases, and any third-party or commercial data sources - together with any system-configuration or data-source inventory documents.

The City has no responsive records to provide.  Please contact the Los Angeles Sheriff's Department for responsive logs and records.



9.   Retention, governance, and training. Records reflecting data-retention periods and deletion practices, access controls (who is authorized to search and what approvals are required), prohibited uses, training materials, and internal policies, standard operating procedures, directives, or general orders governing use of any system identified above.

The City has no responsive records to provide.  Please contact the Los Angeles Sheriff's Department for responsive logs and records.



10.  Misuse, breaches, and oversight. Any audits, reports, internal-affairs records, complaints, disciplinary records, or communications concerning suspected or confirmed misuse of any system (including searches for personal, immigration, or reproductive-health-related reasons), and any records of data breaches or security incidents involving the data.

The City has no responsive records to provide.  Please contact the Los Angeles Sheriff's Department for responsive records.



11. Surveillance-use policy and impact reports. Any Surveillance Use Policy, Surveillance Impact Report, Privacy Impact Assessment / Data Protection Impact Assessment, or comparable document required by any applicable local surveillance-oversight ordinance, relating to ALPR, RTCC, or data-integration technology generally or to a specific vendor.

The City has no responsive records to provide.  Please contact the Los Angeles Sheriff's Department for responsive records.



12. Governing-body review. Staff reports, resolutions, meeting agendas, minutes, and presentations to the city council/ board of supervisors/ oversight body concerning approval, funding, or renewal of any contract identified above.

Please refer back to the PRA folder review: Staff reports 13-B on 7/14/25 and 14-M on 9/22/25.



13.  Confirmation of non-use. If the agency has never used, piloted, or contracted for any ALPR, connected-camera, RTCC, or data-integration system of the kind described above, please confirm In format, preservation and processing."

The City does not have any responsive documents for this request.



This concludes your records request.

Sincerely,

[City Logo]

Juliet Cerecero

Management Assistant

City Clerk's Office

(562) 804-1424 x2104

communications.subject: Indiana Access to Public Records Act Request: Brady Marion County (Marion County Sheriff's Office)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Indiana Access to Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

For the time period of Jan. 1, 2023 through the date this request is fulfilled: materials (including but not limited to memos, reports, lists and personnel records) sent to Indiana prosecutor's office for the purpose to complying with Brady and/or Giglio.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 7 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Emily Hopkins

This message acknowledges that your request has been received and is being processed in accordance with the Indiana Access to Public Records Act, under Ind. Code 5-14-3, et seq. Your request will be reviewed and processed by the City/County agency you’ve selected to determine: 
(1) if the request identifies the public records you seek with “reasonable particularity” (in accordance with Ind. Code 5-14-3-3(a)); 
(2) if the agency has any public records that are responsive to your request; AND 
(3) whether the responsive public records are disclosable to you (in accordance with Ind. Code 5-14-3-4). 
APRA requires City/County agencies to produce responsive and disclosable public records (should they exist) within a reasonable time based upon the circumstances.  If any responsive public records are not disclosable to you, the agency will remove the non-disclosable portion from the public record and provide the statutory basis for any such denial.  Information pertaining to any copying fees (if applicable) will also be provided.

title: (WA ESD 123) All Emails Sent to or Received from mcminimeelaw.com

communications.subject: Washington Public Records Act Request: (WA ESD 123) All Emails Sent to or Received from mcminimeelaw.com
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

All electronic mail sent to or received from any email address operating under
the domain "mcminimeelaw.com" (matching the wildcard string *@mcminimeelaw.com)
exchanged with any district email account, alias, or internal
routing node, acting as either the author, sender, primary recipient,
carbon copy (CC), or blind carbon copy (BCC) holder.

The chronological scope of this request spans the entirety of the District's
available archival retention window.

TECHNICAL PRE-EXCLUSION OF REPETITIVE SYSTEM DATA:

To maximize administrative processing efficiency, accelerate delivery, and
eliminate unnecessary review burdens, the requester explicitly waives
interest in, pre-excludes, and requests the system-level filtering out of
the following non-substantive records categories:

1. Automated calendar invitations, change notifications, or updates.
2. Automated out-of-office or vacation autoreplies generated by either domain.
3. System-generated IT alerts, ticket confirmations, or password actions.

LIMITATION OF SCOPE & PRE-EXCLUSION OF SENSITIVE DATA:

The requester explicitly pre-excludes and waives any interest in the
Personally Identifiable Information (PII) of any individual student under FERPA.

Pursuant to RCW 42.56.210, if the District asserts that specific internal
staff names or student indicators are exempt from disclosure, the District is
required to apply narrow blackouts exclusively to those individual text strings
while releasing the remaining non-exempt text blocks, financial totals,
and generalized policy or administrative discussions.

Blanket withholding of entire records based on broad assertions of privilege
or exempt status is explicitly contested; only the minimal exempt portions
may be withheld.

MANDATORY STATUTORY COMPLIANCE TIMELINE:

As provided by RCW 42.56.520, a formal response is required within five (5)
business days.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Public Interest Mainstreaming Parenting

title: Bruce Sundlun

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Bruce Sundlun
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Records, specifically those unreleased, mentioning or describing Bruce G. Sundlun (born: January 19, 1920 died: July 21, 2011), who was the former governor of Rhode Island.

Please conduct a search of the Central Records System, including but not limited to the Electronic Surveillance (ELSUR) Indices, the Microphone Surveillance (MISUR) Indices, the Physical Surveillance (FISUR) Indices, and the Technical Surveillance (TESUR) Indices, for both main-file records and cross-reference records for all relevant names, individuals, agencies and companies. Please search HQ records as well as ALL field offices and resident agencies.

If any potentially responsive records have been destroyed and/or transferred to NARA, then I request copies of the destruction or transfer slips as well as any other documentation relating to, mentioning or describing said transfer or destruction, to include but not be limited to confirmation that the Bureau has no other copies of said records. If previously released records are available, then I request a rolling release consisting of those records while additional records are located and processed for release.

I am a member of the news media and request classification as such. I have previously written about the government and its activities, and am currently a reporter of The Boston Globe.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Alexa Gagosz

communications.subject: RE: [EXTERNAL EMAIL] -  RE: Freedom of Information Act Request #1647124-000
communications.communication:
Thank you for your inquiry regarding the status of your Freedom of Information Act/Privacy (FOIPA) request.   A review of your request has determined the following:

The request is presently awaiting assignment to a Disclosure analyst who will then review the records to determine if any redactions are required pursuant to subsections of Title 5, U. S. Code, Section 552 and 552a.

You may check the status of your request online at http://vault.fbi.gov by clicking on the ‘Check Status of Your FOI/PA Request’ link. Online status reports are updated weekly.

Requests are processed in the order in which they are received through our multi-track processing system.  Requests are divided into two primary tracks-simple (under 50 pages of potentially responsive documents) and complex (over 50 pages of potentially responsive documents).  Complex requests are further divided into small, medium, large, and extra-large sub-tracks based upon request size.  Simple track extra-small requests typically require the least amount of time to process.  Currently, simple track cases average approximately 230 days from the date of receipt for processing.  Our complex requests in the small processing track are currently averaging 1,085 days, medium processing track are currently averaging 1,310 days, large processing track are currently averaging approximately 2,010 days, and extra-large processing track are currently averaging 2,370 days for processing.

Your request is currently in the complex request medium processing track, and the estimated date of completion for your request is May 2028.  If your request is considered a complex track, considering reducing the scope of your request may accelerate the process as it could potentially place your request in a quicker processing track.  This may also reduce any search and duplication costs, if applicable, and allow for a more timely receipt of your information.

If you wish to discuss reducing the scope of your request, please indicate so and a representative will be in contact.

Respectfully,

Public Information Officer
FBI - Information Management Division
200 Constitution Drive
Winchester, VA  22602
O: (540) 868-4593
E: foipaquestions@fbi.gov<mailto:foipaquestions@fbi.gov>

Do you have further questions about the FOI/PA process? Visit us at http://www.fbi.gov/foia

Please check the status of your request online at https://vault.fbi.gov/fdps-1/@@search-fdps    Status updates are performed on a weekly basis.

Note:  This is a non-emergency email address.  If this is an emergency, please call 911 directly.  If you need to report a tip for immediate action, please contact FBI Tips at http://tips.fbi.gov/ or reach out to your local field office.

title: Subject: Alfredo Shaw File Destruction Logs, Retention Policies, Preservation Records, and Related Communications (Office of the Attorney General - Tennessee)

communications.subject: Tennessee Public Records Act Request: Subject: Alfredo Shaw File Destruction Logs, Retention Policies, Preservation Records, and Related Communications (Office of the Attorney General - Tennessee)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Tennessee Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

To the Public Records Custodian
Shelby County District Attorney General’s Office:

Pursuant to the Tennessee Public Records Act, T.C.A. § 10-7-503 et seq., I request electronic copies of the following existing records concerning Alfredo Bernard Shaw, also known as Alfredo Shaw or Jake Wright.

This request concerns your office’s statement that requested Shaw case files unrelated to Tony Von Carruthers were destroyed on June 25, 2020.

1. Identification of destroyed files

Existing destruction logs, disposal lists, file inventories, case-number lists, database entries, and destruction certificates identifying Shaw files destroyed on June 25, 2020.

Include existing records showing file titles, case numbers, date ranges, record categories, and whether paper or electronic records were destroyed.

2. Authorization and disposal documentation

Existing destruction approvals, authorizations, instructions, work orders, disposal requests, contractor invoices, pickup receipts, and shredding certificates concerning those files.

Date range: January 1–December 31, 2020.

3. Retention policies

Retention schedules, policies, and procedures in effect on June 25, 2020, governing:

* Criminal prosecution files;
* Confidential-informant records;
* Informant payments and benefits;
* Witness credibility and impeachment information;
* Disclosure of evidence to defense attorneys;
* Records associated with appeals and post-conviction proceedings.

Include amendments effective January 1, 2017–June 25, 2020.

4. Preservation notices and legal holds

Existing preservation notices, litigation holds, instructions suspending destruction, and records releasing such holds that applied to Shaw files or records concerning Shaw’s involvement in Carruthers’ case.

Date range: January 1, 1994–October 8, 2026.

5. Communications concerning destruction or preservation

Existing emails, memoranda, letters, and meeting notes concerning the retention, destruction, or preservation of Shaw files, including their relevance to other prosecutions, appeals, post-conviction proceedings, subpoenas, or public-records requests.

Date range: January 1, 2017–December 31, 2020.

6. Surviving copies and transfers

Existing archive indexes, scanning logs, backup catalogs, transfer inventories, receipts, and communications identifying surviving copies of the destroyed Shaw files or transfers of those files to another custodian.

Include records identifying transfers to the Tennessee Attorney General’s Office, courts, law-enforcement agencies, federal agencies, archives, or off-site storage providers.

Date range: January 1, 1994–October 8, 2026.

This item requests existing documentation; it does not request creation of a new inventory or reconstruction of destroyed records.

7. Records supporting the October 2026 response

Existing records relied upon for the statement that Shaw case files unrelated to Carruthers were destroyed on June 25, 2020.

Also provide existing search notes, internal referrals, records-location communications, and approval communications concerning Timothy A. Beacham’s October 2026 response to the Shaw/Carruthers records request.

For records documenting preparation of that response, the date range is October 1–8, 2026. Underlying destruction documentation is requested regardless of its creation date.

8. Communications involving Beacham or Campbell

Existing communications to, from, or copied to Timothy A. Beacham or John Wheeler Campbell concerning the destruction, retention, preservation, location, transfer, or requested disclosure of Shaw files.

Date ranges: January 1, 2017–December 31, 2020, and October 1–8, 2026.

This item is limited to those subjects.

Production Instructions

This request seeks existing records, not answers to questions, legal analysis, or newly created documents.

Please provide electronic records in their existing format where reasonably available, including spreadsheets and electronic logs.

Please release reasonably segregable, nonexempt portions of responsive records. For withheld records or categories, identify the specific legal authority supporting withholding.

Please distinguish records withheld from records not located, destroyed, or maintained by another custodian. If another custodian is known, please identify that office.

Please provide responsive records in installments as they become available. Before incurring charges exceeding $25, please provide an itemized estimate and obtain my authorization.

Please preserve responsive records while this request is being processed.

Respectfully,
Donald Askew Jr.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 7 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Kent Hoover, a citizen of Tennessee, in coordination with Donald R. Askew Jr..

communications.subject: RE: Tennessee Public Records Act Request: Subject: Alfredo Shaw File Destruction Logs, Retention Policies, Preservation Records, and Related Communications (Office of the Attorney General - Tennessee)
communications.communication:
You submitted this request to the Office of the Tennessee Attorney General, but the records you seek are maintained by the Shelby County District Attorney General’s Office.  These are separate agencies, and the Office of the Tennessee Attorney General does not possess the Shelby County District Attorney General’s records.

Please direct your request to the Shelby County District Attorney General’s Office so they may assist you with the records you are seeking.

Thank you.

communications.subject: RE: Tennessee Public Records Act Request: Subject: Alfredo Shaw File Destruction Logs, Retention Policies, Preservation Records, and Related Communications (Office of the Attorney General - Tennessee)
communications.communication:
Thank you for your response.

I understand that the Tennessee Attorney General’s Office and the Shelby County District Attorney General’s Office are separate agencies. However, the Shelby County DA’s Office previously informed me that records associated with Tony Von Carruthers’ pending collateral proceedings are held by the Tennessee Attorney General’s Office. Your response appears inconsistent with that explanation.

Please clarify whether your office possesses any records responsive to my request, including copies received from Shelby County, correspondence, attachments, investigative materials, or records concerning Alfredo Bernard Shaw within the Carruthers case materials.

I am requesting responsive records actually held by your office, including copies, regardless of which agency originally created them. If your response concerns only the DA’s original files, please clarify whether your office separately searched its own holdings.

If your office holds no responsive records, please confirm that a search was conducted and identify the appropriate records custodian or contact so I can resolve these conflicting referrals.

Thank you for helping clarify where these records are maintained.

Donald Askew Jr.

We have run a search for records containing the keywords “Alfredo Bernard Shaw”.  There are too many to send by email so we have set up an FTP site here - https://ftp.ag.tn.gov/login.

These are your login credentials:

ID: daskew
PW: a$7%YQry

Please be sure to download the records you desire to keep as the link will expire in 30 days.

The records on the FTP site represent the non-exempt records.  To the extent there are additional potentially responsive records, they are exempt from public disclosure per TCA 10-7-504(a)(5)(A)(i), (iii), and/or (iv).  We are not required to list or otherwise identify the exempt records.

Thanks for understanding, and have a great rest of the day!

Please include records concerning Shaw’s informant status, payments, benefits, agreements, statements, recantations, and communications relating to Tony Von Carruthers, including copies of FBI, MPD, and Sheriff’s Office records maintained by your office.

I understand your stated position regarding exempt records. Please explain, to the extent possible, the categories withheld and the cited statutory provision applicable to each. Please also confirm whether withheld records were reviewed for non-exempt portions that could be released with redactions.

Finally, please confirm whether the FTP production represents complete responsive files or only keyword-search results, provide the exact access expiration date, and upload the released records here if technically possible. Please do not post the FTP password publicly.

Thank you,

Donald Askew Jr.

Thank you for confirming the production, identifying Document 67 in USDC WDTN Case No. 2:08-cv-02425-JPM-dkv, and advising that the FTP files will remain available until November 14.

For purposes of identifying potentially missing records with specificity, my follow-up concerns the following records, to the extent held by your office:

1. Document 67 and its attachments in the federal case identified above, including the referenced Shelby County Sheriff’s Office document concerning possible payments to Alfredo Bernard Shaw for drug purchases.
2. Records identifying Shaw as an informant, including records bearing FBI identifier 938188EA7, MPD informant number 1069, or Shelby County Sheriff’s Office informant number 2282.
3. Existing payment and benefit records concerning Shaw, including payment vouchers, receipts, agreements, and communications concerning compensation, favorable treatment, dismissal of charges, or other promised benefits connected to his cooperation or testimony against Tony Von Carruthers.
4. The FBI FD-302 dated June 10, 1998, attributed to Special Agent William C. Rasmussen, and records bearing file numbers 282A-ME-50216 or 282B-ME-52439.

Please also clarify whether “several hundred records” refers to individual documents, electronic files, or pages, and whether the FTP production includes all non-exempt attachments to responsive emails.

These requests concern the completeness of the production and the ability to locate specific records within it. I appreciate your assistance as I review the materials.

Respectfully,
Donald Askew Jr.

communications.subject: New Hampshire Right to Know Law Request: Highest-value RFPs (City Clerk's Office)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the New Hampshire Right to Know Law, I hereby request the following records:

Copies of all bids submitted in response to the five highest-value RFPs issued by this agency, with proposal openings between January 1, 2015 and the date this request is fulfilled. Please include any associated records identifying the RFP number, title, and awarded vendor, as well as requests for clarification and communications with the losing bidders.

In some cases, these records may be considered exempt from disclosure because of a privacy interest or some other concern. When considering whether a government record should be released, the courts routinely conduct a balancing test to weigh the public's interest in the records versus the government's interest in non-disclosure. We believe the public interest in these specific records is very high.

Nothing prevents you from making these records available to the public. Both the spirit and letter of the state's Right-to-Know law ensure "the greatest possible public access" to government records and proceedings. We ask that you consider this request carefully and conduct your own balancing test if you are inclined to deny any portion of this request.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Kelly Kauffman

communications.subject: RE: Washington Public Records Act Request #W038325-072226
communications.communication:
Hello,

In your previous communication, you indicated that if I have filed multiple requests, you may wait until the first request is completed before starting to process the next one.

Please be advised of that in the recent ruling in Seattle Times v. City of Seattle (2026), the King County Superior Court ruled that "nothing in the PRA or in caselaw interpreting the PRA supports the notion that a single request should have a lower agency priority simply because it was made by a person who has other pending requests" and that "making public records requests, even voluminous public records requests, is not by itself an unreasonably disruptive or disrespectful act" (referring to  WAC 44-14-01002) and thus ", SPD’s
implementation of MDAR 17-0002 § 5.2.1 [a policy where requests were similarly grouped by requester] does not facilitate timely access to public records and is contrary to law."

I ask that you please confirm that my request is not being unlawfully queued.

Thank you,
Rose

communications.subject: Wisconsin Open Records Act Request: Sheriff use of force data (2017-2025) under 50k population (Jefferson County Sheriff)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Wisconsin Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Use of force (UOF) data dating from January 1, 2017 to December 31, 2025. If possible, please provide this data in database or spreadsheet format and include the case number, incident date, incident time, subject injured indicator, subject injury force related info (e.g. Yes or No), subject age, subject gender, subject ethnicity, subject weapon type, incident area occurred, force type, officer division (e.g. law enforcement operations, detention/correctional operations, etc.), badge number and names associated with the officers involved. If one or more of these fields is unavailable, provide all fields and/or information that is available responsive to my request. If no database or spreadsheet format is available, please provide copies of each individual use of force report or other report where use of force information is documented/reported by officers. Note, this is for all use of force incidents reported by your agency, not limited to only those incidents required to be reported under state or federal programs.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

All records, between the Department and the company Lexipol  (lexipol.com) or its representatives that contain any references to “military equipment” or “AB 481”, including documents, emails and attachments, texts, spreadsheets, recordings, memoranda, and other materials, from July 1, 2024 to the present. 

Records on the Department’s web site indicate that it has used Lexipol templates for at least some policies. 

To assist with the prompt release of responsive material, I ask that you make records available to me as you locate them, rather than waiting until all responsive records have been collected and copied.
 
This request is not being made for commercial purposes.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

John Lindsay-Poland

Dear Ms. Hernandez / Hayward PD staff:

Thank you for your response to my PRA request. I would like to amend (or resubmit, if your agency requires resubmission) my request as follows:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request records (documents, emails and attachments, texts, spreadsheets, recordings) of the Department or its staff containing the following:

Correspondence, purchase orders or contracts between Lexipol Inc. and the Department since January 1, 2022, including attachments to emails, and any policy and report templates provided by Lexipol. 

This request also includes documents downloaded by the Department from Lexipol (lexipol.com), for example from a link provided to APD, and currently possessed by Department staff,  before the Department subsequently changed or adapted them for publication. I am seeking to understand how Lexipol, through its templates, correspondence or other information guides and informs the Department’s policy, especially as regards military equipment policies or annual reports. 

Should you have any questions or concerns regarding this request, please feel free to contact me directly via email at jlindsay-poland@afsc.org or phone at 510-282-8983.  

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely, 
John Lindsay-Poland

title: Case management system procurement records – Journal Technologies (AODA)

communications.subject: New Mexico Inspection of Public Records Act Request: Case management system procurement records – Journal Technologies (AODA)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the New Mexico Inspection of Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Electronic copies of the following existing public records concerning the procurement of a case management system from Journal Technologies, Inc. by the Administrative Office of the District Attorneys, including the FY2026 purchase orders described in state records as "Off the shelf case management system" (approximately $2,325,928 and $800,000):

1. The solicitation document(s) used for this procurement — the Request for Proposals, Invitation to Bid, sole-source determination and posting, or the statewide/cooperative price agreement relied upon — including any addenda and written questions and answers.

2. All proposals, bids, or quotes received in response, including the proposal submitted by Journal Technologies, Inc., with any price schedules or cost proposals.

3. The evaluation committee's scoring sheets, tabulations, and any written evaluation summary or recommendation of award.

4. The notice of award or intent to award, and any protest filed and its resolution.

5. The executed contract or agreement with Journal Technologies, Inc., including all exhibits, statements of work, deliverable and payment schedules, license or subscription terms, service-level terms, and all amendments to date.

6. Any Project Certification Committee (DoIT) certification request forms, project charters, or project management plans submitted for this project.

7. Any implementation schedule, rollout plan, or memorandum identifying which district attorney offices are onboarded to the system and on what dates.

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Unlawfully Delayed MoValley ICE Death Report
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

1. The Congressionally mandated ICE Detainee Death Report for Frankline Okpu, who died December 6, 2023, at the GEO-owned Moshannon Valley ICE Processing Center in Clearfield County, Pennsylvania. 
2. All emails exchanged between ICE and GEO, ICE and CRCL, and ICE and Congress regarding the publication of the Congressionally Mandated Detainee Death Report sent or received between December 6, 2023, and January 24, 2024. 

Expedited Processing Request
Pursuant to 6 CFR 5.5(e), I hereby request expedited processing and certify that the following is true and correct pursuant to 28 USC 1746: 

1. I am a member of the media primarily engaged in information collection and dissemination. 
2. Frankline Okpu died in ICE custody on December 6, 2023. https://www.ice.gov/news/releases/cameroonian-national-ice-custody-dies
3. Implementing Congressional Appropriations requirements, ICE’s death policy, ICE Directive 11003.5, Section 5.3, paragraph 4, mandates ICE make available to the public a detainee death report on its website within 30 days of a person’s death. See https://www.ice.gov/doclib/detention/directive11003-5.pdf. 
4. The ICE Detainee Death Report for a man who died two days before Frankline, Carlos Juan Francisco, is presently online: https://www.ice.gov/doclib/foia/reports/ddr_carlosJuanFrancisco.pdf. 
5. The ICE Detainee Death Report for Frankline is not online as of the date of this request. 
6. Public records received from the Pennsylvania State Police indicate the agency received at least 77 calls for alleged criminal activity at the Moshannon Valley ICE Processing Center between April 2022 and December 2023. https://www.documentcloud.org/documents/24373955-psp_final_response_2023-2559
7. At least 22 of those calls involved allegations of drug paraphernalia or possession. At least 19 of those calls involved allegations of rape, attempted rape, sexual assault, or indecent assault. https://www.documentcloud.org/documents/24373955-psp_final_response_2023-2559. 
8. Frankline Okpu died of a drug overdose—MDMA toxicity—according to toxicology reports by the Clearfield County Coroner’s Report. 
9. Between December 2022 and December 2023, there was not a single month that passed in which the Pennsylvania State Police went without receiving a call to investigate alleged criminal activity at Moshannon Valley. 
10. In June 2023, the Department of Homeland Security’s Office for Civil Rights and Civil Liberties published its May 2023 Closing Memorandum summarizing investigative findings of multiple violations of detention standards at Moshannon Valley. https://www.dhs.gov/sites/default/files/2023-09/23_0620_crcl-close-summary-ice-moshannon-valley-processing-center-06-20-23.pdf. 
11. ICE non-concurred or only partially concurred with at least 20 of 29 of CRCL’s recommendations. 
12. Hundreds of noncitizens currently reside inside involuntarily the Moshannon Valley facility. 
13. Neither ICE nor any of its oversight bodies has publicly released information revealing the cause and manner of Frankline’s death. 

Based on the above, there is an urgent need to inform the public regarding the facts surrounding Mr. Okpu’s death, and the steps the agency may have taken to prevent harm to other people locked inside Moshannon Valley at government expense.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Andrew Free

I hereby request the following records: 1. 2. Effectiveness and Use Statistics All statistical reports, internal summaries, use-justification documents, crime-reduction assessments, or after-action reviews evaluating the effectiveness of Flock Safety cameras since installation. This includes any records prepared in connection with contract renewals. 
3. Cost and Financial Records All financial records related to Flock Safety cameras, including invoices, purchase orders, annual subscription payments, installation costs, and maintenance costs from the date of first installation through the present. Include any records showing federal, state, grant, or civil asset forfeiture funding used to offset costs. 
4. Camera Inventory and Placement The current inventory or deployment list of Flock Safety cameras operated by or accessible to this agency, including number of units and general location descriptions. Also include any written policies, criteria, risk assessments, or internal documents used to determine camera placement locations.

(c) A list of all agencies currently authorized to access this agency's Flock data, including any federal agencies. Please provide these records in their original electronic, machine-readable format (CSV or spreadsheet).

8. Secretary of State Audit All records, correspondence, or internal communications related to the Illinois Secretary of State's 2025 audit of ALPR data-sharing practices, including any communications with the Secretary of State's office or Flock Safety regarding compliance.

Dear Public Access Counselor:

Pursuant to Section 9.5 of the Illinois Freedom of Information Act (FOIA), 5 ILCS 140/9.5, I hereby request review of a public body's failure to respond to a FOIA request as required under 5 ILCS 140/3.

1. Identification of Public Body

City of East Peoria Police Department
East Peoria, IL

2. Date of Original Request

I submitted the FOIA request electronically via the MuckRock platform on August 11, 2026.

3. Summary of Records Sought

The request sought ten categories of records concerning the Department's Flock Safety Automated License Plate Reader (ALPR) system, including, among other things:

• Justification records for the system's adoption
• Effectiveness and use statistics
• Cost and financial records, including any grant or civil asset forfeiture funding
• Camera inventory and placement criteria
• Contracts and data-sharing agreements with Flock Safety
• The Flock "Organization Audit" and "Network Audit" reports documenting searches made within and of the Department's Flock system, and a list of all outside agencies (including federal agencies) authorized to access the Department's ALPR data
• Records of any security incidents or unauthorized access to ALPR data
• Records related to the Illinois Secretary of State's 2025 audit of ALPR data-sharing practices
• Marketing materials and correspondence with Flock Safety

4. Statutory Violation
Under 5 ILCS 140/3(d), a public body must respond to a FOIA request within 5 business days of receipt, or, if a proper written extension notice citing one of the grounds enumerated in 5 ILCS 140/3(e) is provided within that period, within an additional 5 business days. As of the date of this filing, more than five (5) weeks have elapsed since the request was submitted. The Department has:

• Issued no written response, denial, extension notice, or acknowledgment of any kind;
• Failed to respond to a written follow-up inquiry sent on August 26, 2026 (Exhibit B); and
• Failed to respond to a second written follow-up inquiry sent on September 10, 2026 (Exhibit C).

The request status remains "Awaiting Acknowledgement." No fee determination, partial production, or claim of exemption has been communicated. This constitutes a clear violation of 5 ILCS 140/3(d) and, under 5 ILCS 140/9.5(a)-(b), the failure to respond is deemed a denial of the request, ripe for review by this office.

5. Timeliness of This Request for Review

This Request for Review is filed within sixty (60) days of the violation, as required by 5 ILCS 140/9.5(b).

6. Relief Requested

I respectfully request that the Public Access Counselor:

1. Open a Request for Review file and direct the City of East Peoria Police Department to respond immediately to the underlying FOIA request in full;
2. Advise the Department of its obligations under 5 ILCS 140/3 and the consequences of continued noncompliance, including potential civil penalties under 5 ILCS 140/11(j) and referral for further enforcement;
3. Specifically direct production of the Flock "Organization Audit" and "Network Audit" reports (Item 6(a)-(b) of the original request) and the list of outside agencies with data access (Item 6(c)), in the native electronic/machine-readable format originally requested; and
4. Issue a binding opinion, if the Department continues to fail to respond or improperly withholds records, pursuant to 5 ILCS 140/9.5(f)-(g).

7. Link to FOIA request

• https://www.muckrock.com/foi/east-peoria-7760/community-alpr-audit-city-of-east-peoria-il-police-department-218048/

I certify that the foregoing is true and correct to the best of my knowledge.

Respectfully,
Trever Flahaut
9/17/2026

2. Mr. Noviello is the first ICE detainee to die in a BOP facility in over a decade. 
3. His death in BOP's FDC Miami following his imprisonment at Krome Service Processing Center has been the subject of widespread media coverage about which serious questions exist as to the care the government provided him. 
4. ICE's Miami Field Office has overseen the custody and care of at least six (6) people, including Mr. Noviello, who died in ICE custody in FY25--the most of any field office in the United States.
5. An urgent need exists for the public to obtain, review, and understand the circumstances surrounding Mr. Noviello's death in custody as ICE deaths continue to rise to their highest levels since the Covid pandemic and the agency is poised to massively expand ICE detention capacity.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Andrew Free

communications.subject: Public Records Request :: P066761-021826
communications.communication:
Dear Michael Michael: 
Our office received your open records request pursuant to Missouri's Sunshine Law, Chapter 610, RSMo. Your request has been assigned number P066761-021826. The Patrol is committed to adhering to the Sunshine Law and to ensuring that the public obtains access to open records that are not otherwise closed by law. The Sunshine Law requires each public agency to adhere to certain standards. This letter is designed to ensure that you understand our process for fulfilling your records request. Three Business Day Notice Requirement: 
The requested records are not immediately available for dissemination or inspection. The Patrol is required to notify you that additional research time will be required to fulfill the request. This correspondence satisfies the Sunshine Law's notice requirement within the required three business day period. Section 610.023.3, RSMo. 
 Additional Research Time is Required: 
The Patrol receives thousands of open records requests each month. Our Patrol Records Division personnel are dedicated to meeting the intent of Missouri's Sunshine Law and strive to respond to each request in a timely manner. The Patrol operates in all 114 Missouri counties and the independent city of St. Louis. Accordingly, many records maintained by the agency are not centrally located within, or immediately accessible to, the Patrol's Custodian of Records in Jefferson City. Our staff must research your request and ensure that we have captured all responsive records  ̶  regardless of their location within the agency. The research process is time-consuming, but we will make every effort to expedite your request. Estimated Time for Completion: 
The majority of our requests are fulfilled within thirty business days. Some requests require additional research time due to their scope or complexity. Our team will conduct an initial review of your request. If we estimate that the request will be fulfilled within thirty business days, we will not send an updated time estimate. However, if we estimate that the request will take longer than thirty business days, we will provide an updated time estimate that provides a detailed justification for the additional research time. Billing: 
As it relates to billing, Missouri law allows the Patrol to charge fees for copies and research time. Specifically, "[r]esearch time required for fulfilling records requests may be charged at the actual cost of research time." Section 610.026, RSMo. The Missouri Supreme Court recently determined that "staff time is the time required to provide access to public records maintained on computer facilities, recording tapes or disks, videotapes or films, pictures, maps, slides, graphics, illustrations or similar audio or visual items". Gross v. Parson, 624 S.W.3d 877, 884-89 (Mo. 2021) (internal quotations omitted). 
The Patrol will never bill you for redaction time or any research time conducted by our legal staff. You will only be charged for copies and staff research time as permitted by Missouri law. Please let us know if you have questions related to the billing estimate. 
Our team will forward a bill estimate to your attention once we have calculated the permissible costs and fees. The Patrol will not provide the responsive records until receipt of payment. Section 610.026.2, RSMo. 
We appreciate your patience as we review, research, and fulfill your open records request. You can monitor the progress of your request at the link below and you will receive an email when your request has been completed. If you wish to withdraw or clarify your request, or if you have questions, please call our office at (573) 526-6146, or (573) 526-6167. 
 
Sincerely, 
Gerard G. Callahan 
Custodian of Records 
 
Login Link: https://mshp.govqa.us/WEBAPP/_rs/Login.aspx

Missouri sunshine law is very clear about time frames.  The MSHP is very careful to construct their initial response so that they can avoid the 3 business day requirement on all record responses.

Michael

title: Deed Fraud Unit (ROD)

communications.subject: Michigan Freedom of Information Act Request: Deed Fraud Unit (ROD)
communications.communication:
Under the Michigan Freedom of Information Act, I request the following existing records maintained by the Wayne County Register of Deeds concerning the Mortgage and Deed Fraud Unit for Jan. 1, 2016 through the date this request is processed:

- Monthly, quarterly and annual statistical reports showing inquiries or complaints received, cases opened, cases referred for investigation, search warrants, arrest warrants, criminal charges, convictions, cases closed and stolen homes or properties returned.
- The existing records used to calculate or substantiate the cumulative figures currently published on the Register of Deeds’ Mortgage and Deed Fraud Unit webpage: 13,013 inquiries, 2,343 cases opened, 1,172 search warrants, 505 arrest warrants, 347 convictions and 393 stolen homes returned.

This includes any existing spreadsheet, database report, running tally, case log or statistical worksheet used to update those figures. Please provide electronic records in their native format with all existing fields and formulas intact. I am not requesting the creation of a new compilation.

- Existing definitions, written methodologies, policies or instructions explaining what the unit counts as an “inquiry,” “case opened,” “search warrant,” “arrest warrant,” “conviction” and “stolen home returned,” including whether multiple defendants or multiple properties within one investigation are counted separately.
- Records showing when the figures on the webpage were most recently updated and the figures that appeared before each update since Jan. 1, 2016.
- Existing reports showing complaints that were declined, closed without investigation or referred to another agency, including the reason categories used for those dispositions.

If a responsive record contains exempt personal or investigative information, please redact that information and produce all reasonably segregable nonexempt portions. If no responsive record exists for an item, please state that. Electronic records should be provided in their native format where available.
